definition: Clandestine means carried out in deliberate, organized secrecy — hidden because the activity would be stopped or punished if it came to light.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word clandestine. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know clandestine should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Customs finally traced the counterfeit labels to a clandestine workshop that operated only at night, its windows papered over and its machines unbolted for a quick move.
Discreet is the mildest rung and hides nothing at all — a discreet person merely avoids drawing attention — while clandestine work is built, piece by piece, to stay unseen.
Covert is strong but stops short of clandestine: covert work is concealed yet can be perfectly lawful, while clandestine adds the deeper secrecy of an enterprise that would be shut down if found.

Covert means concealed, and covert work can be perfectly official — governments run covert operations with budgets and oversight. Clandestine adds the shadow of the forbidden: hidden not just from view but from authority, because discovery would shut it down.

Surreptitious is stealth in the single act — the note slipped across the desk while the teacher writes, the glance snatched at a rival's cards. Clandestine is stealth as a standing condition: the whole enterprise, meetings and members and records, lives underground.
